newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - BHP shares jump on tax settlement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - BHP shares jump on tax settlement.

text.p: Shares in The Broken Hill Pty Co jumped 11 cents to A$18.05 on Wednesday, their highest level in nearly five months and building on earlier gains, after the company said it had reached agreement with the Victorian state government to resolve a resource rent tax dispute.

Under the settlement, BHP and Esso Australia Resources Ltd, a unit of Exxon Corp, will split A$1 billion with BHP's A$511 million share resulting in an after tax profit of A$167 million. Prior to the announcement of the settlement, BHP shares were trading at A$17.94, up 34 cents.
BHP said A$107 million of the A$167 million related to the period to October 31, 1996, and the balance related to gas to be supplied over the remainder of the current contracts.
"It was obviously better than anticipated," said a Sydney dealer.

The petroleum resource rent tax was imposed by the Federal government on Bass Strait gas production from July 1990. The dispute centred on whether BHP and joint venturer Esso had the right to pass on the tax under contracts with Victorian government-owned entities GASCOR and Generation Victoria.
BHP said the settlement was conditional on final tax and regulatory clearances and the execution of an agreement between the state and Federal government.
By 3.15 p.m. (0400 GMT), BHP shares were 42 cents higher at A$18.02 on turnover of 3.98 million shares.
